notes:
CORRECTION: Skelligs (39) starts on line 3068, not 3067 as given in its row above. Valentia (38) occupies lines 3066-3067.

There are 41 rows, numbered 1-40. "5." is printed twice: once for Dungarvan (line 3027) and once for Coningbeg Lt.-ship (line 3028). Both are kept with number "5". Either Dungarvan was added to the list without renumbering, or the duplicate is a misprint.

How the fields were filled:
- Fragments: leading indentation is stripped; the spacing inside each line is kept as printed. On wrapped rows, the second fragment is the continuation line, also without its indent.
- Name: the comma between name and county is kept when it directly follows the name (e.g. "Fastnet,", "Eagle Island, E.,"), following the "Farn, Inner," example. Strip it if you want clean station names. Where a type comes between name and county ("Coningbeg Lt.-ship, Wexford"), the comma falls after the type, so the name has none.
- Place: printed as is, so "do." (ditto) appears often. Read in order, each "do." stands for the last county named: Co. Cork, Waterford, Wexford, Wicklow, Dublin, Down, Antrim, Donegal, N. Sligo, Mayo, Galway, Clare, Kerry, Cork. Blackrock (27) prints "do" without the full stop. Oyster Island (23) prints "N. Sligo".
- Keepers: the full stop that ends each observer entry is dropped (e.g. "John Whelan"). Pairs joined by "and" are split into two people, including the wrapped ones: "J. Reilly and G. H. / Brownell" and "John Gillan and Robert / Tyrrell".
- Other: holds the Sp./Au. return marks and the miles-from-shore figure, as "Sp. x; Au. o; miles from shore 9". "-" in the miles column probably means a shore station. Samphire Island and Dursey Island are printed "½".
- Dungarvan's Spring column has "-" rather than o or x. The key gives no meaning for "-"; it probably means no schedule was sent that spring (perhaps a station added in autumn), but this is unconfirmed.
- Coast: no sub-headings are printed within the list. "IRISH COAST." is the section heading you gave me; it is not in lines 3014-3080.
- No row has an italic name, *, †, a light character or a light-vessel number. The only types printed are "Lt.-ship" on Coningbeg, Barrels Rock, Arklow S. and Kish Bank. All other rows have no type, though they are lighthouses.

Spellings kept as printed: Innishtrahull (usually Inishtrahull), Howth Baily (Baily lighthouse, Howth), Arranmore, Rathlin O'Birne, Arran Island N. (usually Aran), Tearaght, Valentia, Thomas Sweeny, Barrels Rock.

Points to check for the roll of keepers:
- The same names appear at more than one station. Joseph Hammond is at Mine Head (4) and Rockabill (12). Martin Kennedy is at Old Head, Kinsale (3) and Blackrock (27). Higginbotham is at Dungarvan (Wm.) and Howth (James). Williams appears as Joseph at Broadhaven and Valentia, J. at Blacksod Point and Samphire Island, and Henry at Arranmore. Redmond is at Lough Swilly (Henry) and Eagle Island E. (Robert W.). Keepers moved between stations, so these may or may not be the same people.
- Straw Island (33) and Straw Island, S. (34) are listed as separate stations, with 9 and 6 miles from shore. The miles figure for Straw Island looks odd, since it lies close to Inishmore. Arran Island, N. (32) is also given 9 miles. I copied these as printed.

The abbreviations key follows the list at lines 3071-3074.
